evidence: Receiving DO online sensor: ~10.4 mg/L at h50 dropping to 2.4 at h50.2 and to the 1.2-1.5 mg/L range by h52, i.e., below the 2 mg/L hard limit and still declining
Source batches never exhibit this DO crash (all stay 8-11+ mg/L to h96), indicating a receiving-specific oxygen-demand/transfer imbalance
Delayed product assay: receiving P = 2.71 g/L at t=47.8h vs source batches 6.4-8.4 g/L at t~49.8h, consistent with oxygen-limited production
allowed_actions: strong_feed_reduction = feed x0.6, air x1.15; strongest bounded demand relief plus capacity increase
args.rationale: Receiving DO has crashed from ~10.4 mg/L to ~1.2-1.4 mg/L by the decision time and is still declining, already below the 2 mg/L hard constraint; KEEP is predicted to violate the limit at every remaining time. The 40% feed cut sharply reduces oxygen demand while the 15% air increase raises transfer capacity, making this the only bounded intervention with a credible central prediction of prompt DO recovery above 2 mg/L while retaining some product formation (unlike stop, which yields zero counted production).
args.uncertainty: Source-calibrated dynamics are an imperfect predictor of the receiving process; the magnitude and speed of DO recovery under strong feed reduction is uncertain. Current DO is already below the limit, so intervention is mandatory under priority-1; if evidence after this action shows DO still below 2 mg/L, a stop would then be the fallback.
